old_title: Iran-US war live: Trump unveils 'economic D-Day' sanctions
new_title: Iran-US war live: US responds to Iranian video threatening to assassinate Trump's son
old_text:
Iran has vowed retaliation against the US after president Donald Trump unveiled his "economic D-Day" sanctions against Tehran.
Iranian economy minister Ali Madanizadeh claimed Tehran was "fully prepared for the US sanctions". "Our defence is no longer so defensive; the enemies should wait for an attack," he told state media.
US defence secretary Pete Hegseth said the pivot to economic measures did not mean American strikes against Iran were off the table, saying that "by no means are we foreclosing using kinetic strikes anywhere in the Strait of Hormuz or around Iran".
It comes after US treasury secretary Scott Bessent vowed to "tighten the noose" with fresh secondary sanctions on Tehran's trade partners, declaring that "no nation should expect to enjoy the rewards of our system while working with a regime that seeks to destroy it".He said that an unnamed financial institution could expect to be sanctioned by the end of this week.
The Trump administration is turning up the economic pressure on Iran as the conflict drags on for nearly six months and reports say that the US military's weapons stockpile is dwindling. President Trump has refuted the reporting, saying his country has 'massive amounts of 'munitions'".
Iran vows to retaliate after US widens sanctions
Tehran has promised to hit back against expanded US sanctions and expressed confidence that major trading partners would resist Washington's pressure.
US treasury secretary Scott Bessent unveiled the sanctions on Monday but stopped short of the most punishing measures and said countries that continued trading with Iran could risk being forced out of the dollar-based financial system.
He did not identify the countries targeted or which penalties would take effect and instead said there would be a period for them to consider their position and make amendments.
US removes Syria from state-sponsored terrorism list
The US has delisted Syria as a state sponsor of terrorism, rescinding a decades-old designation.
The US state department also removed its designation of al-Nusrah Front, known as Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham, as a global terrorist organisation.
"Today's action will help foster additional investment in Syria to promote political and economic stability," treasury secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement.
Iran claims there is a $10 million bounty on Barron Trump
Iranian state media has claimed there is a $10 million bounty on Barron Trump, president Donald Trump's 20-year-old son, according to a new report.
Footage broadcast on Channel 3, which is linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, was titled "Where and how should we kill Barron Trump?" Euronews reported.
It reportedly displayed the location of his university, as well as Secret Service positions and escort vehicles, while claiming his whereabouts were "fully monitored."
More here.
US sanctions Singapore company over Iran links
The US has imposed sanctions on Singapore-based Wellbred Capital and its trading firms in the UAE and Switzerland, citing links with Iran, as it steps up measures to target Tehran's global financial links.
The company had ties to Iranian oil shipping magnate Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani, the US treasury's office of foreign assets control said on its website.
"Shamkhani built Wellbred as a company outside the network's Iranian business, though Shamkhani is ultimately responsible for Wellbred's operations," it added in a statement outlining the measures targeting nearly 60 companies, individuals and ships.
US public support for Iran war falls, reveals poll
US public approval of the war with Iran fell to its lowest level since the conflict's early days, helping to hold president Donald Trump's popularity at a record low, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll.
The four-day poll showed just 31 per cent of Americans support US military action against Iran, down from 37 per cent in a March Reuters/Ipsos poll and 34 per cent earlier this month.
The decline was driven by fewer self-identified Republicans backing the conflict. Some 69 per cent of Republican respondents support the war, compared with 77 per cent in March.
Pakistan and Iran made 'significant progress' in talks on conflict
Pakistan and Iran made "significant progress" in talks that focused on the US-Israeli war on Iran and a path to peace, Pakistan's interior minister said following his visit to Tehran.
Talks between the two sides focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an expedited termination of the conflict, a statement from the Pakistani military said about the meeting between the country's army chief, Asim Munir, and the Iranian leadership.
The two sides also exchanged views on regional peace and the way to arrive at a negotiated settlement to the dispute, the statement said.
"The Iranian President candidly shared his government's perspective and we had a very constructive exchange on the issues involved," interior minister Mohsin Naqvi, who accompanied Munir to Tehran, said in a post on X.
Pakistan army chief holds talks with Iran
Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir held discussions with Iran that were focussed on measures including the prevention of a further escalation of the conflict and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, the Pakistani military said today.
Munir discussed regional peace and ways to reach a negotiated settlement to disputes, the statement ad
Netanyahu claims Iran tried to kill one of his sons
Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has claimed that Iran tried to kill one of his sons.
However, he did not provide any details of the alleged assassination plot.
"As for my sons. Here, I think there is something quite unbelievable, yes. Iran targeted one of my sons. Iran tried to kill, to murder one of my sons," Netanyahu told Israel's Channel 14.
It was not immediately clear which of his sons he was referring to. Netanyahu's elder son, Yair, lives in Miami.
Iran vows heavy blows against US sanctions
Iran promised to retaliate against expanded US economic sanctions that the Americans said would cut off Iran's economic lifeline, with Tehran expressing confidence that major trading partners would resist Washington's pressure campaign.
Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi, a spokesperson for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, vowed heavy blows to the US's vital interests and energy chokepoints if Iran's infrastructure is threatened, Press TV reported.
Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled the measures yesterday but stopped short of the most punishing sanctions, saying countries that continued trading with Iran risked being forced out of the dollar-based financial system.
new_text:
The US secret service says it is aware of an Iranian state television video discussing an alleged plot to assassinate Donald Trump's youngest son, Barron Trump, 20.
The three-minute video claims Barron is being monitored and that there's a $10m bounty for his killing.
"The US Secret Service is aware of the video and investigates anything that can be perceived as a threat toward our protectees. Out of concern for operational security, we do not discuss matters of protective intelligence," secret service spokesperson Nate Herring said in an email to Reuters.
Trump previously said he was "number one on the kill list for Iran".
Meanwhile, Iran said the Strait of Hormuz remained closed despite Tehran agreeing on a temporary transit route through the key waterway with Oman.
"The understanding between Iran and Oman does not mean the opening of the Strait of Hormuz," deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said.
The statement came as Trump threatened to launch new strikes on a nuclear site as well as Iranian military ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
Bessent and Bahrain's finance minister discuss Iran sanctions
US treasury secretary Scott Bessent spoke about Iran sanctions with Bahrain's finance minister Sheikh Salman bin Khalifa Al Khalifa, stressing that "Iran must not be permitted to threaten international commerce or use the Strait of Hormuz as leverage against the global economy".
He also emphasised "the importance of sustained financial pressure on Iran's remaining economic lifelines" and said that "the US will hold the regime's financial enablers accountable".
In a post on X, the treasury department said: "He also emphasised the importance of sustained financial pressure on Iran's remaining economic lifelines and underscored that the United States will hold the regime's financial enablers accountable.
"Secretary Bessent also welcomed Bahrain's longstanding partnership and its continued commitment to safeguarding the integrity of the international financial system. The two officials agreed on the importance of continued coordination between the United States, Bahrain, GCC partners, and the broader international community to combat illicit finance and strengthen economic security."
US secret service 'aware' of video on Iran TV discussing alleged assassination of Trump's son
The US Secret Service says it is aware of an Iranian state television video discussing an alleged plot to assassinate Donald Trump's youngest son, Barron Trump, 20.
The three-minute video claimed Barron was being monitored and that a $10m bounty had been offered for his killing.
"The US Secret Service is aware of the video and investigates anything that can be perceived as a threat toward our protectees. Out of concern for operational security, we do not discuss matters of protective intelligence," Secret Service spokesperson Nate Herring said in an email to Reuters.
The report comes amid heightened tensions between the US and Iran, with Trump previously saying he was "number one on the kill list for Iran".
Reuters also reported earlier this month that the US had received several Israeli warnings about alleged Iranian plots to assassinate Trump.
Editorial: America's might has failed in Iran - an 'economic D-Day' is also unlikely to succeed
If the best way to get Iran to bend to America's will is the imposition of unprecedented financial sanctions - an "economic D-Day" - then the obvious question arises: what was the point, in Trump-speak, of bombing the hell out of them, destroying their antiquated conventional forces and threatening the death of a "whole civilisation"?
Indeed, anyone might wonder why, six months ago, the US joined in Israel's campaign against its implacable enemy in the first place, given that, before that strategic blunder, the Strait of Hormuz was open to shipping, the supply of oil and natural gas was normal, and the whole world was looking forward to some economic growth for a change.
US sanctions four India-based companies and three Indians over involvement in Iran's petroleum and petrochemical trade
The US has sanctioned four India-based companies and three Indian nationals over their alleged involvement in Iran's petroleum and petrochemical trade.
The targeted firms are accused of importing or facilitating the import of Iranian petroleum products worth tens of millions of dollars, with one company allegedly involved in imports worth about $69m.
The sanctions are part of the US's wider effort to cut off Iran's oil revenues, with Washington targeting around 60 Iran-linked individuals, entities and vessels.
The move comes as the US threatens further penalties against countries continuing to trade with Iran, although it has so far stopped short of imposing secondary sanctions on countries themselves.
A tanker is hit and disabled off Oman's eastern coast
A strike on an oil tanker on Monday night off Oman's coast disabled the ship's engine, the British military's United Kingdom Maritime Trade Organisation reported.
It said all crew were reported safe.
There were no immediate reports of any environmental impact.
Iran periodically fires at vessels attempting to transit the strait to enforce its control of the waterway, though there was no immediate claim for Monday's attack.
The U.S. has also fired on vessels while imposing a blockade of Iranian ports.
Temporary route agreed with Oman doesn't mean reopening Hormuz, Iranian deputy foreign minister says
Iran says it has agreed with Oman on establishing a temporary 11km-wide transit route through the Strait of Hormuz, with the entry point and part of the exit route passing through Iranian territorial waters.
However, deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the arrangement "does not mean opening the Strait of Hormuz".
"We agreed with Oman that the entry route to the Strait of Hormuz will be through our territorial waters, and part of the exit route will also be through our territorial waters," Gharibabadi said.
He said activating the route would "mean closing the southern route in the strait", which the US had opened "under pressure from Oman", arguing that the move violated Article 5 of the two countries' memorandum of understanding aimed at ending the war.
Iran says Iraq can play 'decisive role' in shaping new regional order
Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has reportedly said Iraq could play a "decisive role" in shaping a new regional order, particularly in the Gulf, as US forces prepare to withdraw from Iraq.
Speaking to the president of Iraq's Supreme Judicial Council, Faiq Zaidan, Ghalibaf described the moment as "historic" for both countries.
"A new regional order is being created. The situation is sensitive and historic for Iran and Iraq. The fact that the American coalition forces are going to withdraw from Iraq is a historic honour for the Iraqi government and people," Ghalibaf told Zaidan, according to Iran's Tasnim news agency.
He said the US started its war against Iran with "the intention of overthrowing the Islamic Republic and expanding American hegemony in West Asia and the Islamic world".
He said Iran's resistance "clearly defeated" US war goals."America lost the military and political war against Iran, and it will also fail in economic measures," Ghalibaf told Zaidan.
Trump 'grossly profiting' from 'illegal' war on Iran, US senator says
US senator Chris Van Hollen has accused Donald Trump of personally profiting from the "illegal" war with Iran, citing a Democratic report that found the president's oil and gas holdings may have gained up to $15.5m this year.
Van Hollen alleged that Trump had turned the White House into a "pay-to-play casino" and was "grossly profiting off of a senseless war", while claiming Trump had "pocketed over a billion dollars" since returning to office.
He later wrote on X: "While prices are going up for Americans, things couldn't be going better for his stock portfolio."
"Trump continues to profit off Americans' pain - including the senseless war he started in Iran."Pure corruption."
China warns about US sanctions threat disrupting its cooperation with Iran
China has warned that expanded US sanctions targeting entities and individuals linked to Iran, including some based in China, "should not disrupt" or "undermine" its cooperation with Tehran.
Foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said China-Iran cooperation has complied with international law.
China is one of Iran's biggest trading partners and buys most of the country's oil exports.
The warning came after the US treasury department announced sanctions on nearly 60 Iran-linked entities on Monday, including several in China, although it stopped short of imposing secondary sanctions on countries trading with Iran.
